fix(markup): a style tag spans a plugin pair it encloses (rich-markup-cg6)

The plugin-aware walk rendered the text between plugin pairs as separate
built-in parses, so every style tag closed at the first pair's boundary and
its closing tag then matched nothing: '[bold]x[click]y[/click]z[/bold]'
threw "doesn't match any open tag" with [bold] visibly open. Since gfr let
[/] close a plugin tag, '[bold][aa]x[/][/]' threw the same way, and an
unclosed '[bold]pre [aa]x[/aa] post' silently lost bold after the pair.

Each plugin pair's handler output now takes the pair's place in one built-in
walk over the slice, so an enclosing style covers it like plain text and the
handler's own spans repaint it as an inner tag would. The same change stops
a base style from painting over markup colours whenever a plugin pair is
present, which the final whole-output stylize used to do.

A style tag that opens on one side of a plugin pair's boundary and closes on
the other has no span to give, since the handler replaces the text inside;
the pairing walk now rejects it with an error naming the plugin boundary.

feat(widgets): hit-test the painted frame; widgets get their own coordinates (rich-runtime-fna.2) (#192)

* feat(widgets): hit-test the painted frame; widgets get their own coordinates (rich-runtime-fna.2)

WidgetBase.render stamps a subclass's `draw` output with its anchor, so the
frame a screen paints is its own hit map. `widgetAt(frame, x, y)` names the
innermost widget under a cell and the cell's place in that widget's output;
EventRouter reads it off `FrameSource.frame` and delivers each pointer event
in the widget's own coordinates, a captured drag relative to the origin its
press found. `bounds`, `WidgetBounds`, `containsPoint`, the active-overlay
set and the z-sorted `widgets` getter are gone: z-order is paint order, and
the overlay pass stamps overlay row i as the widget's row footprint+i.

* fix(widgets): a widget owns its rectangle; drags follow the repainted widget; releases know if they landed (rich-runtime-fna.2)

- WidgetBase.render pads every row to the widest and terminates each row,
  so a click past a short row still hits and a blank last row survives.
- Captured drags read the widget's origin off the current frame (originOf).
- WidgetMouseEvent carries `over`; the parser's event is ScreenMouseEvent.
  Dropdown reads `over` instead of recomputing its own extent.
- Segment.anchorLines takes firstRow; the overlay pass drops its pad/slice.

* fix(widgets): only a WidgetBase mounts; a release dragged off a click widget cancels it (rich-runtime-fna.2)

MountEntry and Screen move to screen.ts so the entry type can name
WidgetBase without types.ts depending upward on it.

fix(markup): halve the backslash run in front of a tag, as Rich does (rich-markup-nm1)

TAG_RE's \[ alternative read any backslash-bracket pair as an escape, so
\\[red]hi[/red] lost its opening tag and threw on the close. The parser now
captures the run and halves it like _parse; escape() doubles it like the
reference's escape. The string is tokenized once and plugin splicing selects
tokens by position, so a run at a plugin boundary is halved too.
